note: The Byzantine Empire and the Khazar Khaganate maintained a consistent alliance against their shared enemies: the Islamic Umayyad and Abbasid Caliphates and, later, the Bulgars. Byzantine emperors cemented the alliance through dynastic marriages: Constantine V married a Khazar princess (Tzitzak, baptized Eirene), making his son Leo IV 'the Khazar.' The Khazars' conversion to Judaism (traditionally dated c. 740) did not disrupt the alliance; Byzantium valued the Khazars as a buffer on the northern Black Sea steppe. The Khazars' eventual destruction by Sviatoslav I of Kiev (965) removed the Byzantine steppe buffer and directly contributed to the Pecheneg pressure on Byzantium.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Byzantine-Khazar alliance demonstrates Byzantine grand strategy of maintaining buffer states on every frontier through diplomacy and dynastic marriage; the destruction of the Khazar buffer by Kiev is a strategic disaster for Byzantium — the Pechenegs and Cumans who replace the Khazars are far more threatening and less diplomatically manageable
